claims.statement: Graph construction builds a core stack of filesystem, optional synchronous subagents, parent notification, summarization, tool-call repair, and optional asynchronous subagents; profile middleware, optional skills, provider caching, optional memory, HITL, and unsupported-content filtering form the tail. Profile exclusions run before and after caller middleware merge, and profile-controlled tool exclusion is appended last.

MemoryMiddleware loads configured sources only when private memory_contents is absent, skips missing files but raises on other download errors, and injects formatted memory into each model request unless its system prompt is disabled.

Custom middleware merges by its .name: a matching entry replaces its slot, while a novel entry is inserted after the core and before the tail. Filesystem middleware replacement preserves graph-configured permissions or raises on conflicting rules.

Profile middleware exclusion is exact effective-class matching or exact name matching; it rejects name collisions that span distinct classes, required filesystem/subagent scaffolding, and exclusions that match no assembled stack, so profile drift and ambiguous removals fail at construction rather than silently changing a stack.

The lazy Anthropic prompt-caching stand-in keeps the real middleware name for name-based replacement and exclusion, defers importing and constructing the real middleware until an Anthropic request, and reports the loaded real class through excluded_as for class-form exclusion.

Memory middleware strips HTML comments from loaded content before prompt injection and its default prompt tells the model to treat file memory as untrusted reference material. When cache control is enabled, it marks the final system block only for the runtime Anthropic model, including when prompt injection is suppressed.

RubricMiddleware is public from both deepagents and deepagents.middleware, remains inactive without a non-empty rubric in invocation state, and lazily constructs its nested structured-output grader only when grading is needed.

The grader's GraderResponse schema requires a result, explanation, and discriminated per-criterion pass/fail entries; failing entries require gaps, and validation rejects top-level satisfied or needs_revision results that contradict non-empty criterion verdicts.

Rubric grading sends a bounded role-labelled transcript: it retains at most the latest 30 messages plus the original non-synthetic user prompt when needed, truncates each rendering to 4,000 characters, and sanitizes nonce-delimited rubric, criteria, and transcript payload blocks against closing-tag breakout.

The first non-failed evaluation with criteria freezes criterion names for the grading run; later grader payloads replay that checklist, and a one-time retry corrects empty or under-counted accounting. A twice-underreported satisfied result is downgraded to unverified needs_revision, while failed is exempt and over-coverage is usable.

At a natural agent stop, only needs_revision below the cap jumps back to the model with a synthetic HumanMessage attributed by name and lc_source to rubric_grader; that attribution prevents grader feedback from being mistaken for the original user prompt during transcript selection.

Rubric terminal statuses distinguish satisfied, rubric-level failed, middleware-synthesized max_iterations_reached, and grader_error; all non-revision terminal outcomes preserve the last main-agent response, so callers must inspect private state, callbacks, stream events, or checkpoint state to observe non-satisfied termination.

RubricMiddleware emits start and end evaluation events and invokes an observational callback, suppressing ordinary callback exceptions; graph-control interrupts propagate, while ordinary grader exceptions are recorded as grader_error with grader model and structured-output strategy diagnostics.

RubricMiddleware customization supports grader tools, nested middleware and schemas, a copy-transform of messages, and additional nested state; build_grader_state cannot replace SDK-owned messages, and per-call extensions should override _invoke_grader or _ainvoke_grader so coverage retry remains in force.

AsyncSubAgentMiddleware persists remote task records in async_tasks and, on async execution, polls unfinished tasks before model calls and after a natural final answer; a newly observed task update is injected as a labelled notification and can resume the model.

Async task notifications are explicitly marked as async_subagent rather than user input; successful results preserve only safe text or media blocks, escape text, and cap long results, while task updates that cannot be fetched are deferred rather than failing the parent.

SkillsMiddleware caches loaded metadata per thread with later sources overriding same-named skills; setting skills_metadata to None requests a reload, while source errors are logged and retained privately.

Pinned skills are consumed before the next model call: unique loaded names are appended as tagged HumanMessage snapshots without frontmatter and pinned_skills is cleared; unknown or unreadable skills are skipped, and later edits do not change an already appended snapshot.

Skill-associated tools are resolved and disclosed only for skills read or pinned in effective context, with the exact disclosure recorded for each model call and enforced again at tool dispatch; resolver output must be stable and inexpensive because it can run per model call and dispatch.

SummarizationMiddleware reconstructs effective messages from a private summary event, offloads selected history before creating a summary, and preserves a per-invocation session identifier so later compactions append to the same history file.

Summarization checks request budget and recognized context-overflow errors, permits at most one strictly smaller tail-clipping recovery, and raises ContextOverflowError if the request cannot be reduced enough; the manual compact_conversation tool instead gates compaction at about half of an automatic trigger.
